source.text: וּמֹשֶׁ֗ה הָיָ֥ה רֹעֶ֛ה אֶת־צֹ֛אן יִתְר֥וֹ חֹתְנ֖וֹ כֹּהֵ֣ן מִדְיָ֑ן וַיִּנְהַ֤ג אֶת־הַצֹּאן֙ אַחַ֣ר הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר וַיָּבֹ֛א אֶל־הַ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים חֹרֵֽבָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Moses was shepherding [the] flock of Jethro his father-in-law, [the] priest of Midian, and he drove the flock behind the wilderness and came to [the] mountain of God, to Horeb.

en.L: And Moses was shepherding the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian; and he drove the flock to the far side of the wilderness and came to the mountain of God, to Horeb.
en.B: Moses was looking after the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian. He led the flock deep into the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.
en.R: Moses took care of the sheep and goats that belonged to his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian. One day Moses led the animals far into the desert. He came to Horeb, the mountain of God.

es.L: Y Moisés estaba pastoreando el rebaño de Jetro, su suegro, el sacerdote de Madián; y llevó el rebaño al otro lado del desierto y llegó al monte de Dios, a Horeb.
es.B: Moisés cuidaba el rebaño de su suegro Jetro, el sacerdote de Madián. Llevó el rebaño hasta lo más lejano del desierto y llegó a Horeb, el monte de Dios.
es.R: Moisés cuidaba las ovejas y las cabras de su suegro Jetro, el sacerdote de Madián. Un día llevó los animales muy lejos, al desierto. Así llegó a Horeb, el monte de Dios.

fr.L: Et Moïse faisait paître le troupeau de Jéthro, son beau-père, le prêtre de Madian ; et il mena le troupeau à l’autre bout du désert et vint à la montagne de Dieu, à l’Horeb.
fr.B: Moïse gardait le troupeau de son beau-père Jéthro, le prêtre de Madian. Il conduisit le troupeau loin dans le désert et arriva à l’Horeb, la montagne de Dieu.
fr.R: Moïse s’occupait des moutons et des chèvres de son beau-père Jéthro, le prêtre de Madian. Un jour, il a emmené les bêtes loin dans le désert. Il est arrivé à l’Horeb, la montagne de Dieu.

sw.L: Naye Musa alikuwa akichunga kundi la Yethro baba mkwe wake, kuhani wa Midiani; akaliongoza kundi hadi upande wa mbali wa nyika, akafika kwenye mlima wa Mungu, Horebu.
sw.B: Musa alikuwa akichunga kundi la baba mkwe wake Yethro, kuhani wa Midiani. Akaliongoza kundi mbali ndani ya nyika, akafika Horebu, mlima wa Mungu.
sw.R: Musa alikuwa akiwatunza kondoo na mbuzi wa baba mkwe wake Yethro, kuhani wa Midiani. Siku moja Musa aliwapeleka wanyama hao mbali jangwani. Akafika Horebu, mlima wa Mungu.

vi.L: Và Môi-se đang chăn bầy chiên của Giê-trô, cha vợ ông, thầy tế lễ Ma-đi-an; và ông dẫn bầy chiên đến phía bên kia hoang mạc và đến núi của Đức Chúa Trời, đến Hô-rếp.
vi.B: Môi-se đang chăn bầy chiên dê của cha vợ mình là Giê-trô, thầy tế lễ xứ Ma-đi-an. Ông dẫn bầy vào sâu trong hoang mạc và đến Hô-rếp, núi của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Môi-se chăn bầy chiên dê cho cha vợ là Giê-trô, thầy tế lễ xứ Ma-đi-an. Một hôm Môi-se dẫn bầy vật đi xa vào hoang mạc. Ông đến Hô-rếp, là núi của Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그리고 모세는 자기 장인, 곧 미디안의 제사장 이드로의 양 떼를 치고 있었다. 그가 양 떼를 광야 저편으로 몰고 가다가 하나님의 산, 호렙에 이르렀다.
ko.B: 모세는 미디안의 제사장인 장인 이드로의 양 떼를 돌보고 있었다. 그는 양 떼를 몰고 광야 깊숙이 들어가다가 하나님의 산인 호렙에 이르렀다.
ko.R: 모세는 장인 이드로의 양과 염소를 돌보았다. 이드로는 미디안의 제사장이었다. 어느 날 모세는 짐승들을 몰고 광야 멀리까지 들어갔다. 그러다가 하나님의 산인 호렙에 이르렀다.

pt.L: E Moisés apascentava o rebanho de Jetro, o seu sogro, sacerdote de Midiã; e conduziu o rebanho para o outro lado do deserto e chegou ao monte de Deus, a Horebe.
pt.B: Moisés cuidava do rebanho do seu sogro Jetro, sacerdote de Midiã. Ele levou o rebanho para o interior do deserto e chegou a Horebe, o monte de Deus.
pt.R: Moisés cuidava das ovelhas e cabras do seu sogro Jetro, o sacerdote de Midiã. Um dia, Moisés levou os animais para bem longe, deserto adentro. Ele chegou a Horebe, o monte de Deus.

decisions.choice: Jethro: the priest of Midian, called Reuel in 2:18
decisions.reason: The same man has two names in Exodus (2:18; 3:1). He may have had a personal name and a title, or Reuel may be the name of his clan.

decisions.choice: behind the wilderness: to the far side of the wilderness, or westward into it
alternatives: to the west side of the wilderness
decisions.reason: "Behind" can mean "beyond", or "west", since a Hebrew speaker faced east to give directions. Either way, Moses went far from the usual pastures.

decisions.choice: the mountain of God, Horeb: the mountain called Sinai elsewhere
decisions.reason: Horeb and Sinai are names for the same mountain (compare 19:11 with Deuteronomy 5:2). The narrator calls it "the mountain of God" because of what happens there; its location is not certain.

decisions.choice: desert
decisions.reason: The "wilderness" is dry, empty land used for grazing. Readable uses the common word.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("il mena", "arriva"); passé composé at Readable ("il a emmené", "il est arrivé")
decisions.reason: The passé simple is the tense of written French narrative; Readable uses the passé composé, the tense of spoken French and of school reading today. The ongoing shepherding at the start is in the imperfect ("faisait paître", "gardait") at every level.

decisions.choice: "광야" (wilderness) at Readable too
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "광야" at every level; it is a plain, familiar word in Korean, so Readable does not need the English Readable's "desert".

decisions.choice: "Giê-trô"; "hoang mạc" at every level; "Hô-rếp"
decisions.reason: The terms note's forms. "Hoang mạc" is the wild, thinly grassed land where flocks can graze, which "sa mạc" (sand desert) is not; Readable keeps it too, since it is a common word.

decisions.choice: Jetro; o monte de Deus; Horebe
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "Jetro" is the usual Brazilian form of Jethro, Reuel's other name (m1); "Horebe" is the form docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md gives, and the mountain is "o monte" here and at Sinai (19:2 on), the word Portuguese uses for a holy mountain (m3).

source.text: וַ֠יֵּרָא מַלְאַ֨ךְ יְהֹוָ֥ה אֵלָ֛יו בְּלַבַּת־אֵ֖שׁ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַסְּנֶ֑ה וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֤ה הַסְּנֶה֙ בֹּעֵ֣ר בָּאֵ֔שׁ וְהַסְּנֶ֖ה אֵינֶ֥נּוּ אֻכָּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And appeared [the] angel of Yahweh to him in [a] flame of fire from [the] midst of the bush, and he looked, and look, the bush [was] burning with fire, and the bush was not consumed.

en.L: And the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of the bush. And he looked, and look, the bush was burning with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
en.B: There the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to him in a flame of fire coming out of a bush. Moses looked, and although the bush was ablaze, it was not burning away.
en.R: There the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to him in a fire that was burning inside a bush. Moses looked closely. The bush was on fire, but the fire did not destroy it.

es.L: Y el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se le apareció en una llama de fuego desde el medio de la zarza. Y miró, y he aquí que la zarza estaba ardiendo con fuego, y la zarza no quedaba consumida.
es.B: Allí el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se le apareció en una llama de fuego que salía de una zarza. Moisés miró, y aunque la zarza estaba en llamas, el fuego no la consumía.
es.R: Allí el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino a él en un fuego que ardía dentro de una zarza. Moisés miró con atención. La zarza estaba en llamas, pero el fuego no la destruía.

fr.L: Et l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} lui apparut dans une flamme de feu, du milieu du buisson. Et il regarda, et voici, le buisson était en feu, et le buisson n’était pas dévoré.
fr.B: Là, l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} lui apparut dans une flamme de feu qui sortait d’un buisson. Moïse regarda : le buisson flambait, et pourtant il ne se consumait pas.
fr.R: Là, l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est venu vers lui dans un feu qui brûlait au milieu d’un buisson. Moïse a regardé attentivement. Le buisson était en feu, mais le feu ne le détruisait pas.

sw.L: Na malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamtokea katika mwali wa moto kutoka katikati ya kichaka. Akatazama, na tazama, kichaka kilikuwa kikiwaka moto, na kichaka hakikuungua.
sw.B: Huko malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamtokea katika mwali wa moto uliokuwa ukitoka kichakani. Musa akatazama, akaona kwamba ingawa kichaka kilikuwa kikiwaka, hakikuteketea.
sw.R: Huko malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimjia katika moto uliokuwa ukiwaka ndani ya kichaka. Musa akatazama kwa makini. Kichaka kilikuwa kinawaka moto, lakini moto haukukiharibu.

vi.L: Và thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hiện ra với ông trong ngọn lửa từ giữa bụi gai. Và ông nhìn, và kìa, bụi gai cháy trong lửa, mà bụi gai không bị thiêu rụi.
vi.B: Tại đó thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hiện ra với ông trong một ngọn lửa từ giữa bụi gai. Môi-se nhìn, thấy bụi gai đang cháy rực mà không hề bị thiêu rụi.
vi.R: Tại đó thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với ông trong ngọn lửa cháy giữa một bụi cây gai. Môi-se nhìn kỹ. Bụi gai đang cháy, nhưng lửa không thiêu hủy nó.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 떨기나무 가운데서 나오는 불꽃 속에서 그에게 나타났다. 그가 보니, 보라, 떨기나무에 불이 붙어 타고 있는데도 그 떨기나무가 타 없어지지 않았다.
ko.B: 거기서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 떨기나무 가운데서 타오르는 불꽃 속에서 그에게 나타났다. 모세가 보니, 떨기나무에 불이 붙었는데도 나무가 타서 없어지지 않았다.
ko.R: 거기서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 떨기나무 속에서 타오르는 불 가운데 모세에게 나타났다. 모세는 자세히 보았다. 떨기나무에 불이 붙어 있었지만, 나무는 타 버리지 않았다.

pt.L: E o anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} lhe apareceu numa chama de fogo do meio da sarça. E ele olhou, e eis que a sarça ardia no fogo, e a sarça não se consumia.
pt.B: Ali o anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} lhe apareceu numa chama de fogo que saía de uma sarça. Moisés olhou e viu que a sarça estava em chamas, mas não se consumia.
pt.R: Ali o anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a ele num fogo que ardia dentro de uma sarça, um arbusto com espinhos. Moisés olhou bem. A sarça estava pegando fogo, mas o fogo não a destruía.

decisions.choice: the angel of Yahweh: God's messenger, in whom God himself is present
decisions.reason: The word means "messenger". In the next verses it is God himself who speaks from the bush (verses 4-6), as with the angel in Genesis 16:7-13 and 22:11-16. The text does not explain how the messenger and God are related.

decisions.choice: the bush: a thorny desert shrub
decisions.reason: The word is used only here and in Deuteronomy 33:16. It sounds like "Sinai", the name of the mountain, a link that may be intended.

decisions.choice: flame of fire: fire marks God's presence
decisions.reason: Fire goes with God's appearances: the smoking firepot (Genesis 15:17), the pillar of fire (13:21), and the fire on Sinai (19:18).

decisions.choice: angel
decisions.reason: "Angel" is the familiar word for God's heavenly messenger. "Messenger" is given in the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: el SEÑOR (default); Yahvé (divine name setting)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Exodus, as in Genesis. As in English, the name is written "el SEÑOR" in capitals, following long custom, to set it apart from the title "Señor"; at the start of a sentence it is "El SEÑOR". The divine name setting shows "Yahvé", the usual Spanish form of the name in scholarship (also spelled "Yahveh" or "Yavé"). "Jehová", familiar to Spanish readers from the Reina-Valera tradition, joins the consonants of the name to the vowels of the word for Lord, and is not used. Because a personal name takes no article in Spanish, the setting span takes in the article and its contractions with a preposition: "el SEÑOR" / "Yahvé", "del SEÑOR" / "de Yahvé", "al SEÑOR" / "a Yahvé". This holds throughout the book.

decisions.choice: le SEIGNEUR (default); Yahvé (divine name setting)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Exodus, as in Genesis. As in English, the name is written "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals, to set it apart from the title "Seigneur"; at the start of a sentence it is "Le SEIGNEUR". The divine name setting shows "Yahvé", the usual French form of the reconstructed name. "L'Éternel", the rendering of the Segond tradition, is a form a reviewer may prefer: it echoes the link with the verb "to be" (3:14) but is a title rather than the name, and it is not the default. Since a name takes no article in French, the span takes in the article and its contractions: "le SEIGNEUR" / "Yahvé", "du SEIGNEUR" / "de Yahvé", "au SEIGNEUR" / "à Yahvé". "The LORD God" is "le SEIGNEUR Dieu", and Adonai YHWH "le Seigneur DIEU".

decisions.choice: "n'était pas dévoré"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is "to eat": fire "eats" what it burns. Literal keeps the picture with "dévoré"; Balanced uses the usual "se consumer".

decisions.choice: BWANA (default); Yahwe (divine name setting)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Exodus, as in Genesis. As in English, the name is written "BWANA" in capitals, to set it apart from the title "Bwana". The divine name setting shows "Yahwe", the reconstructed form of the name in Swahili spelling. "Yehova", known to Swahili readers from some churches, joins the consonants of the name to the vowels of the word for Lord, and is not used. Swahili has no article, so the span is the name alone; "the LORD God" is "BWANA Mungu", and Adonai YHWH "Bwana MUNGU".

decisions.choice: "kichaka" (bush, shrub)
decisions.reason: The word is a thorny desert shrub (m2). "Kichaka" is the everyday word for a bush; "kijiti" suggests a small stick or sapling.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}" for YHWH, with the particle outside the span
decisions.reason: Book-wide, as the Korean style guide (section 7a) and the Genesis sheet set: the default "주" (the LORD) and the alternative "야훼" both end in a vowel, so one particle (의, 께서, 께) fits both.

decisions.choice: "떨기나무" (bush)
decisions.reason: The established Korean word for this bush, as Korean Acts 7:30, 35 has it.

decisions.choice: "thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}"; "bụi gai"
decisions.reason: The Genesis terms note's phrase for the angel of the LORD, with the divine_name span; the bush is a thorny shrub (meaning decision), which "bụi gai" names.

decisions.choice: o anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as in Genesis and docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md: the name is "o SENHOR" in capitals by default, "Javé" with the divine name setting, and the article and its contraction go inside the span ("do SENHOR" / "de Javé"), since "o Javé" is not Portuguese. "Jeová" is not used.

decisions.choice: a sarça; R adds "um arbusto com espinhos" the first time
decisions.reason: For the whole book (3:2-4; Deuteronomy 33:16): "sarça" is the Portuguese word for a thorny desert shrub (m2) and the name by which readers know this scene. Readable keeps it and explains it once, "um arbusto com espinhos", as a new reader may not know the word.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה אָסֻֽרָה־נָּ֣א וְאֶרְאֶ֔ה אֶת־הַמַּרְאֶ֥ה הַגָּדֹ֖ל הַזֶּ֑ה מַדּ֖וּעַ לֹא־יִבְעַ֥ר הַסְּנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses, let me turn aside and see this great sight, why does not burn the bush?

en.L: And Moses said, "Let me turn aside, please, and see this great sight, why the bush does not burn up."
en.B: Moses said, "I must turn aside and look at this remarkable sight. Why is the bush not burning away?"
en.R: Moses said to himself, "This is amazing! I will go over and look at it. Why does the bush not burn up?"

es.L: Y dijo Moisés: «Voy a apartarme, pues, y ver este gran espectáculo: por qué no se consume la zarza».
es.B: Moisés dijo: «Tengo que acercarme a mirar esto tan extraordinario. ¿Por qué la zarza no se quema del todo?».
es.R: Moisés se dijo: «¡Qué asombroso! Voy a ir a verlo de cerca. ¿Por qué no se quema la zarza?».

fr.L: Et Moïse dit : « Je vais donc faire un détour et voir ce grand spectacle : pourquoi le buisson ne brûle pas. »
fr.B: Moïse dit : « Il faut que je fasse un détour pour regarder ce spectacle extraordinaire. Pourquoi le buisson ne se consume-t-il pas ? »
fr.R: Moïse s’est dit : « C’est étonnant ! Je vais m’approcher pour regarder. Pourquoi le buisson ne brûle-t-il pas jusqu’au bout ? »

sw.L: Musa akasema, "Na nigeuke kando sasa, nikaone jambo hili kubwa, kwa nini kichaka hakiungui."
sw.B: Musa akasema, "Lazima niende kando nikaangalie jambo hili la ajabu. Kwa nini kichaka hiki hakiteketei?"
sw.R: Musa akajiambia, "Hili ni la kushangaza! Nitakwenda kuliangalia. Kwa nini kichaka hakiungui?"

vi.L: Và Môi-se nói: "Ta hãy rẽ qua mà xem cảnh tượng lớn lạ này, tại sao bụi gai không cháy hết."
vi.B: Môi-se nói: "Mình phải lại gần xem cảnh tượng lạ lùng này mới được. Tại sao bụi gai không cháy tiêu?"
vi.R: Môi-se tự nhủ: "Lạ quá! Mình phải đến xem mới được. Tại sao bụi gai không cháy rụi?"

ko.L: 그리고 모세가 말하였다. "내가 이제 돌이켜 가서 이 큰 광경을, 어찌하여 떨기나무가 타 없어지지 않는지 보아야겠다."
ko.B: 모세는 "내가 가서 이 놀라운 광경을 보아야겠다. 어째서 떨기나무가 타 버리지 않는 것일까?" 하고 말하였다.
ko.R: 모세는 혼잣말을 했다. "참 놀라운 일이다! 가까이 가서 보아야겠다. 왜 떨기나무가 타 버리지 않을까?"

pt.L: E Moisés disse: "Vou agora me desviar e ver esta grande visão: por que a sarça não se queima."
pt.B: Moisés disse: "Preciso ir até lá e ver esta coisa extraordinária. Por que a sarça não se consome?"
pt.R: Moisés disse consigo mesmo: "Que coisa espantosa! Vou até lá ver isso. Por que a sarça não se queima toda?"

decisions.choice: turn aside: leave his path to go and look
decisions.reason: Verse 4 uses the same verb: God speaks when he sees that Moses has turned aside. The meeting begins with Moses' curiosity.

decisions.choice: said to himself
decisions.reason: No one else is present, so Moses is speaking to himself.

decisions.choice: "Ta hãy" (L); "Mình phải" (B)
decisions.reason: Moses speaks to himself; Vietnamese uses "ta" or "mình" for oneself in thought, where "tôi" would need a hearer.

source.text: וַיַּ֥רְא יְהוָ֖ה כִּ֣י סָ֣ר לִרְא֑וֹת וַיִּקְרָא֩ אֵלָ֨יו אֱלֹהִ֜ים מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַסְּנֶ֗ה וַיֹּ֛אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֥ה מֹשֶׁ֖ה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Yahweh that he turned aside to see, and called to him God from [the] midst of the bush and said, Moses, Moses. And he said, here I [am].

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saw that he turned aside to see, and God called to him from the midst of the bush and said, "Moses, Moses!" And he said, "Here I [am]."
en.B: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saw that he had come over to look, God called out to him from the bush: "Moses! Moses!" "Yes, I am here," he answered.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} saw that Moses had come to look. So God called to him from inside the bush, "Moses! Moses!" Moses answered, "Yes, I am here."

es.L: Y vio {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} que se apartaba para mirar, y Dios lo llamó de en medio de la zarza y dijo: «¡Moisés, Moisés!». Y él dijo: «Aquí estoy».
es.B: Cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vio que Moisés se había acercado a mirar, Dios lo llamó desde la zarza: «¡Moisés! ¡Moisés!». «Sí, aquí estoy», respondió él.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vio que Moisés se acercaba a mirar. Entonces Dios lo llamó desde dentro de la zarza: «¡Moisés! ¡Moisés!». Moisés respondió: «Sí, aquí estoy».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vit qu’il faisait un détour pour voir, et Dieu l’appela du milieu du buisson et dit : « Moïse, Moïse ! » Et il dit : « Me voici. »
fr.B: Quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vit qu’il s’était approché pour regarder, Dieu l’appela du buisson : « Moïse ! Moïse ! » « Oui, me voici », répondit-il.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a vu que Moïse venait regarder. Alors Dieu l’a appelé du milieu du buisson : « Moïse ! Moïse ! » Moïse a répondu : « Oui, je suis là. »

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipoona kwamba amegeuka kando ili kutazama, Mungu akamwita kutoka katikati ya kichaka, akasema, "Musa, Musa!" Naye akasema, "Mimi hapa."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipoona kwamba amekuja kutazama, Mungu akamwita kutoka kichakani, "Musa! Musa!" Akajibu, "Naam, mimi hapa."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliona kwamba Musa amekuja kutazama. Basi Mungu akamwita kutoka ndani ya kichaka, "Musa! Musa!" Musa akajibu, "Naam, niko hapa."

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thấy ông rẽ qua để xem, thì Đức Chúa Trời gọi ông từ giữa bụi gai và phán: "Môi-se, Môi-se!" Và ông thưa: "[Có] con đây."
vi.B: Khi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thấy ông lại gần để xem, Đức Chúa Trời từ giữa bụi gai gọi ông: "Môi-se! Môi-se!" Ông thưa: "Dạ, con đây."
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thấy Môi-se đến xem. Vì vậy Đức Chúa Trời từ trong bụi gai gọi ông: "Môi-se! Môi-se!" Môi-se thưa: "Dạ, con đây."

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그가 보려고 돌이켜 오는 것을 보셨고, 하나님께서 떨기나무 가운데서 그를 부르시며 말씀하셨다. "모세야, 모세야!" 그러자 그가 말하였다. "제가 [여기] 있습니다."
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세가 보려고 다가오는 것을 보시고, 하나님께서 떨기나무 가운데서 그를 부르셨다. "모세야! 모세야!" 모세가 대답하였다. "예, 제가 여기 있습니다."
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 모세가 보려고 다가오는 것을 보셨다. 그래서 하나님께서 떨기나무 속에서 모세를 부르셨다. "모세야! 모세야!" 모세가 대답했다. "예, 제가 여기 있습니다."

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} viu que ele se desviava para ver, e Deus o chamou do meio da sarça e disse: "Moisés, Moisés!" E ele disse: "Eis-me aqui."
pt.B: Quando {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} viu que ele tinha ido olhar, Deus o chamou do meio da sarça: "Moisés! Moisés!" "Aqui estou", respondeu ele.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} viu que Moisés tinha vindo olhar. Então Deus o chamou de dentro da sarça: "Moisés! Moisés!" Moisés respondeu: "Sim, estou aqui."

decisions.choice: Yahweh ... God: the same one, called by both names
decisions.reason: The verse moves between the divine name and "God" without a change of subject. The name will be explained in verses 14-15.

decisions.choice: here I am: an answer of readiness
decisions.reason: This is the answer of Abraham when God called him (Genesis 22:1, 11) and of Jacob (Genesis 46:2). It means "I am listening, ready."

decisions.choice: Moses, Moses: the name is said twice
decisions.reason: God calls Abraham, Jacob and Samuel the same way (Genesis 22:11; 46:2; 1 Samuel 3:10), at a moment that changes their lives.

decisions.choice: God speaks to Moses in 해라체 with "나" and "너"; Moses answers God in 합쇼체 with "저/제"
decisions.reason: As the Genesis sheet sets for God and people; it holds for every exchange between God and Moses in Exodus.

decisions.choice: Moses to God: "con" for himself, "Chúa" or "Ngài" for God; God to Moses: "Ta", and "ngươi" (L) or "con" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Genesis terms note's forms for God and a person, recorded once for these chapters; "phán" is kept for God speaking.

decisions.choice: Eis-me aqui (L); Aqui estou (B); Sim, estou aqui (R)
decisions.reason: The answer of readiness (m2) takes the same three forms as in Genesis 22:1 and 46:2, where Abraham and Jacob give it, so the echo is kept in Portuguese.

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אַל־תִּקְרַ֣ב הֲלֹ֑ם שַׁל־נְעָלֶ֨יךָ֙ מֵעַ֣ל רַגְלֶ֔יךָ כִּ֣י הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתָּה֙ עוֹמֵ֣ד עָלָ֔יו אַדְמַת־קֹ֖דֶשׁ הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, do not come near here; take off your sandals from on your feet, for the place which you [are] standing on it is ground of holiness.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Do not come near here. Take your sandals off your feet, for the place on which you are standing is ground of holiness."
en.B: "Come no nearer," God said. "Remove your sandals from your feet, because the place where you stand is holy ground."
en.R: God said, "Do not come any closer. Take off your sandals. You are standing on holy ground, because I am here."

es.L: Y dijo: «No te acerques aquí. Quítate las sandalias de los pies, porque el lugar en el que tú estás de pie es tierra de santidad».
es.B: «No te acerques más», dijo Dios. «Quítate las sandalias de los pies, porque el lugar donde te encuentras es tierra santa».
es.R: Dios le dijo: «No te acerques más. Quítate las sandalias. Estás pisando tierra santa, porque yo estoy aquí».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Ne t’approche pas d’ici. Enlève tes sandales de tes pieds, car l’endroit où tu te tiens, c’est une terre de sainteté. »
fr.B: « Ne viens pas plus près, dit Dieu. Retire les sandales de tes pieds, car l’endroit où tu es debout est une terre sainte. »
fr.R: Dieu a dit : « Ne t’approche pas plus. Enlève tes sandales. Tu es sur une terre sainte, parce que je suis ici. »

sw.L: Akasema, "Usisogee hapa. Vua makubazi yako kutoka miguuni mwako, kwa sababu mahali unaposimama juu yake ni ardhi ya utakatifu."
sw.B: Mungu akasema, "Usikaribie zaidi. Vua makubazi yako, kwa sababu mahali unaposimama ni ardhi takatifu."
sw.R: Mungu akasema, "Usije karibu zaidi. Vua makubazi yako. Umesimama juu ya ardhi takatifu, kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niko hapa."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán: "Đừng đến gần đây. Hãy cởi dép khỏi chân ngươi, vì nơi ngươi đang đứng là đất thánh."
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời phán: "Đừng lại gần nữa. Hãy cởi dép ra khỏi chân con, vì chỗ con đang đứng là đất thánh."
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời phán: "Đừng lại gần hơn nữa. Hãy cởi dép ra. Con đang đứng trên đất thánh, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang ở đây."

ko.L: 그리고 그분께서 말씀하셨다. "이리로 가까이 오지 말아라. 네 발에서 신을 벗어라. 네가 서 있는 곳은 거룩한 땅이다."
ko.B: 하나님께서 말씀하셨다. "더 가까이 오지 말아라. 네 발에서 신을 벗어라. 네가 서 있는 곳은 거룩한 땅이다."
ko.R: 하나님께서 말씀하셨다. "더 가까이 오지 말아라. 신을 벗어라. 내가 여기 있으니, 네가 서 있는 땅은 거룩한 곳이다."

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse: "Não te aproximes daqui. Tira as tuas sandálias dos teus pés, porque o lugar em que estás é terra de santidade."
pt.B: "Não te aproximes mais", disse Deus. "Tira as sandálias dos pés, porque o lugar onde estás é terra santa."
pt.R: Deus disse: "Não chegues mais perto. Tira as sandálias. Estás pisando em terra santa, porque eu estou aqui."

decisions.choice: holy ground: set apart because God is present
decisions.reason: The ground is not holy in itself; it is holy because God is there. This is the first time Exodus uses the word "holy". Joshua is given the same command in Joshua 5:15.

decisions.choice: take off your sandals: a sign of respect
decisions.reason: Removing sandals shows reverence. Israel's priests seem to have served barefoot in the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: God said
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he said". Balanced and Readable name the speaker, avoiding a pronoun at the start of the sentence.

decisions.choice: because I am here
decisions.reason: Readable says why the ground is holy, which the context makes clear.

decisions.choice: "makubazi" (sandals)
decisions.reason: The word is sandals, the footwear of a shepherd. "Viatu" is shoes in general.

decisions.choice: "đất thánh" at every level
decisions.reason: "Ground of holiness" is a Hebrew way of saying holy ground; Vietnamese "đất thánh" is the natural phrase, even at Literal.

decisions.choice: tu (God to Moses): "Não te aproximes", "Tira", "estás"
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as in Genesis (13:14): God speaks to one person with "tu", so his words to Moses read "te", "teu", "contigo" and the second person singular at every level; when he speaks to Moses with the elders or the people, he says "vocês" (3:12, 18-22). The negative imperative takes the subjunctive, "Não te aproximes", "Não chegues".

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אָנֹכִי֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י אָבִ֔יךָ אֱלֹהֵ֧י אַבְרָהָ֛ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִצְחָ֖ק וֵאלֹהֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֑ב וַיַּסְתֵּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ פָּנָ֔יו כִּ֣י יָרֵ֔א מֵהַבִּ֖יט אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, I [am the] God of your father, [the] God of Abraham, [the] God of Isaac and [the] God of Jacob. And hid Moses his face, for he was afraid of looking at God.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I [am] the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob." And Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.
en.B: Then God said, "I am the God your father worshiped, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob." Moses covered his face, for he was afraid to look upon God.
en.R: God said, "I am the God your father worshiped. I am the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob." When Moses heard this, he hid his face. He was afraid to look at God.

es.L: Y dijo: «Yo [soy] el Dios de tu padre, el Dios de Abraham, el Dios de Isaac y el Dios de Jacob». Y Moisés se cubrió el rostro, porque tuvo miedo de mirar a Dios.
es.B: Luego Dios dijo: «Yo soy el Dios a quien adoraba tu padre, el Dios de Abraham, de Isaac y de Jacob». Moisés se tapó la cara, porque temía mirar a Dios.
es.R: Dios dijo: «Yo soy el Dios a quien adoraba tu padre. Soy el Dios de Abraham, de Isaac y de Jacob». Al oír esto, Moisés escondió la cara. Tenía miedo de mirar a Dios.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Je [suis] le Dieu de ton père, le Dieu d’Abraham, le Dieu d’Isaac et le Dieu de Jacob. » Et Moïse se cacha le visage, car il avait peur de regarder Dieu.
fr.B: Puis Dieu dit : « Je suis le Dieu que ton père adorait, le Dieu d’Abraham, d’Isaac et de Jacob. » Moïse se couvrit le visage, car il craignait de regarder Dieu.
fr.R: Dieu a dit : « Je suis le Dieu que ton père adorait. Je suis le Dieu d’Abraham, d’Isaac et de Jacob. » Quand Moïse a entendu cela, il s’est caché le visage. Il avait peur de regarder Dieu.

sw.L: Akasema, "Mimi [ni] Mungu wa baba yako, Mungu wa Abrahamu, Mungu wa Isaka, na Mungu wa Yakobo." Naye Musa akajifunika uso, kwa sababu aliogopa kumtazama Mungu.
sw.B: Kisha Mungu akasema, "Mimi ni Mungu ambaye baba yako alimwabudu, Mungu wa Abrahamu, wa Isaka na wa Yakobo." Musa akajifunika uso wake, kwa kuwa aliogopa kumwangalia Mungu.
sw.R: Mungu akasema, "Mimi ni Mungu ambaye baba yako alimwabudu. Mimi ni Mungu wa Abrahamu, Isaka na Yakobo." Musa aliposikia hivyo, akaficha uso wake. Aliogopa kumtazama Mungu.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán: "Ta [là] Đức Chúa Trời của cha ngươi, Đức Chúa Trời của Áp-ra-ham, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sác và Đức Chúa Trời của Gia-cốp." Và Môi-se che mặt mình, vì ông sợ nhìn Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán: "Ta là Đức Chúa Trời mà cha con đã thờ phượng, Đức Chúa Trời của Áp-ra-ham, của Y-sác và của Gia-cốp." Môi-se che mặt lại, vì ông sợ nhìn thấy Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời phán: "Ta là Đức Chúa Trời mà cha con đã thờ phượng. Ta là Đức Chúa Trời của Áp-ra-ham, Y-sác và Gia-cốp." Nghe vậy, Môi-se che mặt lại. Ông sợ nhìn thấy Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그리고 그분께서 말씀하셨다. "나는 네 아버지의 하나님, 아브라함의 하나님, 이삭의 하나님, 야곱의 하나님이다." 그러자 모세가 자기 얼굴을 가렸으니, 하나님을 바라보기가 두려웠기 때문이다.
ko.B: 하나님께서 말씀하셨다. "나는 네 아버지가 섬기던 하나님, 곧 아브라함과 이삭과 야곱의 하나님이다." 모세는 하나님을 뵙기가 두려워서 얼굴을 가렸다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 말씀하셨다. "나는 네 아버지가 섬기던 하나님이다. 나는 아브라함과 이삭과 야곱의 하나님이다." 이 말씀을 듣고 모세는 얼굴을 가렸다. 하나님을 바라보기가 두려웠기 때문이다.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse: "Eu [sou] o Deus do teu pai, o Deus de Abraão, o Deus de Isaque e o Deus de Jacó." E Moisés escondeu o rosto, porque tinha medo de olhar para Deus.
pt.B: Então Deus disse: "Eu sou o Deus a quem o teu pai adorava, o Deus de Abraão, de Isaque e de Jacó." Moisés cobriu o rosto, pois tinha medo de olhar para Deus.
pt.R: Deus disse: "Eu sou o Deus que o teu pai adorava. Eu sou o Deus de Abraão, de Isaque e de Jacó." Quando ouviu isso, Moisés escondeu o rosto. Ele tinha medo de olhar para Deus.

decisions.choice: your father: singular, Moses' own father, or the forefathers as one
decisions.reason: The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Septuagint read the plural "your fathers", as in verses 13 and 15. The Hebrew singular may mean Moses' father Amram, or the line of fathers taken together.

decisions.choice: the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob: the God who made promises to them
decisions.reason: God names himself by the people he made his covenant with (2:24). Jesus quotes these words in Mark 12:26 to show that God is the God of the living.

decisions.choice: afraid to look at God: no one can see God and live
decisions.reason: Compare Genesis 32:30, Exodus 33:20 and Judges 13:22.

decisions.choice: the God your father worshiped
decisions.reason: "The God of your father" means the God whom your father served. Balanced and Readable say so, to avoid suggesting a family god owned by one man.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה רָאֹ֥ה רָאִ֛יתִי אֶת־עֳנִ֥י עַמִּ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וְאֶת־צַעֲקָתָ֤ם שָׁמַ֨עְתִּי֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י נֹֽגְשָׂ֔יו כִּ֥י יָדַ֖עְתִּי אֶת־מַכְאֹבָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh, seeing I have seen [the] affliction of my people who [are] in Egypt, and their cry I have heard because of their taskmasters, for I know their pains.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "I have surely seen the affliction of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people who [are] in Egypt, and I have heard their outcry because of their taskmasters, for I know their pains.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "I have taken full note of the misery of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people in Egypt. I have heard them cry out under their taskmasters. I know how they are suffering.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "I have seen how badly {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people in Egypt are being treated. I have heard them crying out because of the cruel men who make them work. I know how much they are hurting.

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: «He visto, sí, he visto la aflicción de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo que [está] en Egipto, y he oído su clamor a causa de sus capataces, porque conozco sus dolores.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: «He observado bien la miseria de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo en Egipto. He oído cómo gritan bajo sus capataces. Sé lo que están sufriendo.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: «He visto lo mal que tratan a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo en Egipto. Los he oído gritar por culpa de los hombres crueles que los obligan a trabajar. Sé cuánto están sufriendo.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit : « J’ai bien vu l’affliction de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple qui [est] en Égypte, et j’ai entendu leur cri à cause de leurs chefs de corvée, car je connais leurs souffrances.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit : « J’ai pris pleinement connaissance de la misère de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple en Égypte. Je les ai entendus crier sous la contrainte de leurs chefs de corvée. Je sais combien ils souffrent.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit : « J’ai vu comme on maltraite {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple en Égypte. Je les ai entendus crier à cause des hommes cruels qui les forcent à travailler. Je sais combien ils ont mal.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Kuona nimeona taabu ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} walioko Misri, na kilio chao nimekisikia kwa sababu ya wanyapara wao, kwa kuwa ninajua uchungu wao.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Nimeiona kikamilifu dhiki ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} huko Misri. Nimewasikia wakilia chini ya wanyapara wao. Ninajua jinsi wanavyoteseka.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Nimeona jinsi watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wanavyoteswa huko Misri. Nimewasikia wakilia kwa sababu ya watu wakatili wanaowalazimisha kufanya kazi. Ninajua jinsi wanavyoumia.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Ta đã thật thấy nỗi khốn khổ của dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở Ai Cập, và đã nghe tiếng kêu than của họ vì những kẻ cai dịch, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} biết những nỗi đau đớn của họ.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Ta đã thấy rõ nỗi khốn khổ của dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở Ai Cập. Ta đã nghe tiếng họ kêu than dưới tay những kẻ cai dịch. Ta biết họ đau khổ thế nào.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Ta đã thấy dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở Ai Cập bị đối xử tàn tệ ra sao. Ta đã nghe họ kêu khóc vì những kẻ độc ác bắt họ làm việc. Ta biết họ đau khổ biết bao.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다. "내가 이집트에 있는 내 백성의 고통을 똑똑히 보았고, 그들의 감독들 때문에 [터져 나오는] 그들의 부르짖음을 들었다. 내가 그들의 아픔을 알고 있다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다. "나는 이집트에 있는 내 백성이 겪는 고통을 똑똑히 보았다. 감독들에게 시달리며 부르짖는 소리도 들었다. 나는 그들이 얼마나 괴로운지 알고 있다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다. "나는 이집트에 있는 내 백성이 얼마나 심하게 학대받는지 보았다. 그들을 억지로 일하게 하는 잔인한 감독들 때문에 그들이 울부짖는 소리도 들었다. 나는 그들이 얼마나 아파하는지 안다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse: "Certamente vi a aflição do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo que [está] no Egito, e ouvi o seu clamor por causa dos seus capatazes, porque conheço os seus sofrimentos.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} disse: "Eu vi muito bem a miséria do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo no Egito. Ouvi o seu clamor por causa dos capatazes. Sei o quanto eles estão sofrendo.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} disse: "Eu vi como o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo está sendo maltratado no Egito. Ouvi o povo gritando por causa dos homens cruéis que o obrigam a trabalhar. Sei o quanto eles estão sofrendo.

decisions.choice: seeing I have seen: the verb is doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: Hebrew strengthens a verb by repeating it: "I have truly seen", "I have seen it all".

decisions.choice: seen ... heard ... know: God's answer to 2:24-25
decisions.reason: The verbs of 2:24-25 (heard, saw, knew) return, now spoken by God himself.

decisions.choice: my people: Israel belongs to God
decisions.reason: This is the first time God calls Israel "my people". It is the claim behind the demand to Pharaoh: "Let my people go" (5:1).

decisions.choice: taskmasters: drivers who forced the work
decisions.reason: The word is used of those who press or drive others to work; it is a different word from the officers of 1:11.

decisions.choice: "He visto, sí, he visto"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the doubled verb of the Hebrew (m1) by repeating it.

decisions.choice: "Kuona nimeona"
decisions.reason: Swahili can strengthen a verb by putting its infinitive before it, as Hebrew does (m1). Literal keeps the doubled verb.

decisions.choice: "đã thật thấy" (L); "đã thấy rõ" (B)
decisions.reason: The doubled verb is for emphasis (meaning decision); Vietnamese shows it with an adverb, since repeating the verb would not read as emphasis.

decisions.choice: "những kẻ cai dịch" for taskmasters
decisions.reason: Drivers who forced the work (meaning decision); "cai dịch" names men set over forced labor, and "kẻ" shows the narrator's view of them.

decisions.choice: os capatazes
decisions.reason: For the whole book (3:7; 5:6-14): the drivers who forced the work (m4) are "capatazes", the plain word for a man who drives a gang of workers; "exatores" is a tax word most readers do not know. It is kept apart from the officers of forced labor of 1:11 ("chefes de trabalhos forçados") and from the Israelite foremen of 5:6 ("supervisores"), as the Hebrew keeps them apart. Readable says what they did, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וָאֵרֵ֞ד לְהַצִּיל֣וֹ׀מִיַּ֣ד מִצְרַ֗יִם וּֽלְהַעֲלֹתוֹ֮ מִן־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַהִוא֒ אֶל־אֶ֤רֶץ טוֹבָה֙ וּרְחָבָ֔ה אֶל־אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָ֑שׁ אֶל־מְק֤וֹם הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ וְהַ֣חִתִּ֔י וְהָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י וְהַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I have come down to deliver it from [the] hand of Egypt and to bring it up from that land to [a] land good and broad, to [a] land flowing [with] milk and honey, to [the] place of the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Amorite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite.

en.L: And I have come down to deliver them from the hand of Egypt and to bring them up from that land to a good and broad land, to a land flowing [with] milk and honey, to the place of the Canaanites and the Hittites and the Amorites and the Perizzites and the Hivites and the Jebusites.
en.B: I have come down to rescue them from the power of Egypt and to lead them up out of that country into a fine, wide land, a land flowing with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
en.R: So I have come down to save them from the Egyptians. I will lead them out of Egypt and bring them to a good land with plenty of room. It is a rich and fertile land, full of milk and honey. The Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites live there now.

es.L: Y he descendido para librarlo de la mano de Egipto y para hacerlo subir de esa tierra a una tierra buena y amplia, a una tierra que fluye leche y miel, al lugar de los cananeos, los hititas, los amorreos, los ferezeos, los heveos y los jebuseos.
es.B: He descendido para rescatarlos del poder de Egipto y sacarlos de ese país hacia una tierra buena y espaciosa, una tierra que fluye leche y miel, donde ahora viven los cananeos, los hititas, los amorreos, los ferezeos, los heveos y los jebuseos.
es.R: Por eso he bajado para salvarlos de los egipcios. Los voy a sacar de Egipto y los llevaré a una tierra buena, con mucho espacio. Es una tierra rica y fértil, llena de leche y miel. Allí viven ahora los cananeos, los hititas, los amorreos, los ferezeos, los heveos y los jebuseos.

fr.L: Et je suis descendu pour le délivrer de la main de l’Égypte et pour le faire monter de ce pays-là vers un pays bon et vaste, vers un pays où coulent le lait et le miel, vers le lieu des Cananéens, des Hittites, des Amoréens, des Phéréziens, des Héviens et des Jébusiens.
fr.B: Je suis descendu pour le délivrer du pouvoir de l’Égypte et le faire monter de ce pays vers un pays bon et vaste, un pays où coulent le lait et le miel, là où vivent maintenant les Cananéens, les Hittites, les Amoréens, les Phéréziens, les Héviens et les Jébusiens.
fr.R: Alors je suis descendu pour les sauver des Égyptiens. Je vais les faire sortir d’Égypte et les conduire dans un bon pays, où il y a beaucoup de place. C’est un pays riche et fertile, où coulent le lait et le miel. Les Cananéens, les Hittites, les Amoréens, les Phéréziens, les Héviens et les Jébusiens y habitent maintenant.

sw.L: Nami nimeshuka ili kuwaokoa kutoka mkononi mwa Misri, na kuwapandisha kutoka nchi ile hadi nchi nzuri na pana, hadi nchi itiririkayo maziwa na asali, hadi mahali pa Wakanaani, na Wahiti, na Waamori, na Waperizi, na Wahivi, na Wayebusi.
sw.B: Nimeshuka ili kuwaokoa kutoka katika nguvu za Misri na kuwapandisha kutoka nchi ile kwenda nchi nzuri na yenye nafasi kubwa, nchi itiririkayo maziwa na asali, mahali wanapoishi sasa Wakanaani, Wahiti, Waamori, Waperizi, Wahivi na Wayebusi.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nimeshuka ili niwaokoe kutoka kwa Wamisri. Nitawatoa Misri na kuwaleta katika nchi nzuri yenye nafasi tele. Ni nchi tajiri yenye rutuba, iliyojaa maziwa na asali. Wakanaani, Wahiti, Waamori, Waperizi, Wahivi na Wayebusi wanaishi huko sasa.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã ngự xuống để giải cứu họ khỏi tay Ai Cập và đem họ lên khỏi xứ ấy đến một xứ tốt và rộng, đến xứ tràn đầy sữa và mật, đến nơi của người Ca-na-an, người Hê-tít, người A-mô-rít, người Phê-rê-sít, người Hê-vít và người Giê-bu-sít.
vi.B: Ta đã xuống để giải cứu họ khỏi quyền lực của người Ai Cập và đưa họ ra khỏi xứ ấy, đến một xứ tốt đẹp và rộng rãi, xứ tràn đầy sữa và mật, là nơi người Ca-na-an, người Hê-tít, người A-mô-rít, người Phê-rê-sít, người Hê-vít và người Giê-bu-sít đang sống.
vi.R: Vì vậy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã xuống để cứu họ khỏi tay người Ai Cập. Ta sẽ đưa họ ra khỏi Ai Cập và dẫn họ đến một xứ tốt đẹp, rộng rãi. Đó là một xứ màu mỡ, tràn đầy sữa và mật. Hiện nay người Ca-na-an, người Hê-tít, người A-mô-rít, người Phê-rê-sít, người Hê-vít và người Giê-bu-sít đang sống ở đó.

ko.L: 그래서 내가 내려왔다. 이집트의 손에서 그들을 건져 내고, 그 땅에서 그들을 이끌어 좋고 넓은 땅, 젖과 꿀이 흐르는 땅, 곧 가나안 사람과 헷 사람과 아모리 사람과 브리스 사람과 히위 사람과 여부스 사람이 사는 곳으로 올라가게 하려는 것이다.
ko.B: 그래서 내가 그들을 이집트의 손아귀에서 건져 내려고 내려왔다. 그들을 그 땅에서 이끌어 내어 좋고 넓은 땅, 젖과 꿀이 흐르는 땅으로 데려가겠다. 그곳은 지금 가나안 사람과 헷 사람과 아모리 사람과 브리스 사람과 히위 사람과 여부스 사람이 사는 곳이다.
ko.R: 그래서 나는 그들을 이집트 사람들에게서 구해 내려고 내려왔다. 나는 그들을 이집트에서 이끌어 내어 넓고 좋은 땅으로 데려가겠다. 그 땅은 기름지고 풍성하여 젖과 꿀이 넘쳐흐른다. 지금은 가나안 사람과 헷 사람과 아모리 사람과 브리스 사람과 히위 사람과 여부스 사람이 그곳에 살고 있다.

pt.L: E desci para livrá-lo da mão do Egito e para fazê-lo subir daquela terra para uma terra boa e espaçosa, para uma terra onde corre leite e mel, para o lugar dos cananeus, e dos hititas, e dos amorreus, e dos ferezeus, e dos heveus, e dos jebuseus.
pt.B: Por isso desci para libertá-lo do poder do Egito e fazê-lo subir daquela terra para uma terra boa e ampla, uma terra onde corre leite e mel, onde agora vivem os cananeus, os hititas, os amorreus, os ferezeus, os heveus e os jebuseus.
pt.R: Por isso desci para salvar o povo dos egípcios. Vou tirá-lo do Egito e levá-lo para uma terra boa e espaçosa. É uma terra rica e fértil, cheia de leite e mel. Os cananeus, os hititas, os amorreus, os ferezeus, os heveus e os jebuseus vivem lá agora.

decisions.choice: I have come down: God acts in the world
decisions.reason: God "comes down" to see and to act (Genesis 11:5; 18:21). It does not mean God was absent before.

decisions.choice: flowing with milk and honey: a rich land
decisions.reason: Milk from flocks and herds, and honey (wild bees' honey or syrup from dates or figs), stand for a land of plenty. This is the first of many times the phrase is used of Canaan.

decisions.choice: the Canaanites ... Jebusites: the peoples living in Canaan
decisions.reason: Lists like this one name the peoples of the land promised to Abraham (Genesis 15:18-21). The names are singular in Hebrew, standing for each people as a whole.

decisions.choice: the hand of Egypt: Egypt's power
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for control or power.

decisions.choice: a rich and fertile land
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture before giving it.

decisions.choice: "le délivrer", "le faire monter" (singular, the people)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pronoun is singular, referring to "my people" in verse 7. French keeps the singular with "peuple"; Readable says "les", the Israelites themselves.

decisions.choice: "xứ tràn đầy sữa và mật"; the six peoples as "người Ca-na-an", "người Hê-tít", ...
decisions.reason: The terms note's forms, used through these books.

decisions.choice: livrá-lo, fazê-lo subir (the people as "it")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the people with a singular pronoun. Portuguese can do the same after "o meu povo", so Literal and Balanced say "livrá-lo" where the English needs "them"; the sense is the same.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֕ה הִנֵּ֛ה צַעֲקַ֥ת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּ֣אָה אֵלָ֑י וְגַם־רָאִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת־הַלַּ֔חַץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִצְרַ֖יִם לֹחֲצִ֥ים אֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And now look, [the] cry of [the] sons of Israel has come to me, and also I have seen the oppression which Egypt [is] oppressing them.

en.L: And now look, the cry of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel has come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I have also seen the oppression with which the Egyptians are oppressing them.
en.B: The outcry of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} has now reached {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I have seen how harshly the Egyptians are crushing them.
en.R: Now I have heard the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} crying out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And I have seen how cruelly the Egyptians are treating them.

es.L: Y ahora, he aquí, el clamor de los hijos de Israel ha llegado hasta {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y también he visto la opresión con que los egipcios los oprimen.
es.B: El clamor de los israelitas ha llegado ahora hasta {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y he visto con qué dureza los aplastan los egipcios.
es.R: Ahora he oído a los israelitas clamar a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Y he visto con qué crueldad los tratan los egipcios.

fr.L: Et maintenant, voici, le cri des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël est venu jusqu’à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et j’ai vu aussi l’oppression dont les Égyptiens les oppriment.
fr.B: Le cri des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} est maintenant parvenu jusqu’à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et j’ai vu avec quelle dureté les Égyptiens les écrasent.
fr.R: Maintenant, j’ai entendu les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} crier vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Et j’ai vu avec quelle cruauté les Égyptiens les traitent.

sw.L: Basi sasa, tazama, kilio cha wana wa Israeli kimefika {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} pia nimeona dhuluma ambayo Wamisri wanawadhulumu nayo.
sw.B: Kilio cha Waisraeli sasa kimenifikia, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nimeona jinsi Wamisri wanavyowakandamiza vikali.
sw.R: Sasa nimewasikia Waisraeli wakinililia. Tena nimeona jinsi Wamisri wanavyowatendea kwa ukatili.

vi.L: Và bây giờ, kìa, tiếng kêu than của con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên đã thấu đến {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng đã thấy sự áp bức mà người Ai Cập áp bức họ.
vi.B: Bây giờ tiếng kêu than của dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã thấu đến {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã thấy người Ai Cập đè nén họ khắc nghiệt thế nào.
vi.R: Bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nghe dân Y-sơ-ra-ên kêu cầu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ta cũng đã thấy người Ai Cập đối xử tàn ác với họ thế nào.

ko.L: 그리고 이제 보아라, 이스라엘 자손의 부르짖음이 내게 이르렀고, 이집트 사람들이 그들을 억누르는 그 억압도 내가 보았다.
ko.B: 이제 이스라엘 백성의 울부짖음이 내게 들려왔다. 이집트 사람들이 그들을 얼마나 혹독하게 짓누르는지도 내가 보았다.
ko.R: 이제 나는 이스라엘 사람들이 나에게 울부짖는 소리를 들었다. 이집트 사람들이 그들을 얼마나 잔인하게 대하는지도 보았다.

pt.L: E agora, eis que o clamor dos filhos de Israel chegou a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, e também vi a opressão com que os egípcios os oprimem.
pt.B: O clamor dos israelitas chegou agora até {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, e vi com que dureza os egípcios os esmagam.
pt.R: Agora eu ouvi os israelitas clamando a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. E vi com quanta crueldade os egípcios os tratam.

decisions.choice: cry: an outcry for help against injustice
decisions.reason: The word is the cry of those wronged, as the outcry against Sodom (Genesis 18:20-21). Here it comes from the oppressed.

decisions.choice: the oppression ... oppressing: pressing, squeezing
decisions.reason: The verb means to press hard against (Numbers 22:25). The Egyptians are crushing Israel; the law forbids Israel to treat foreigners this way (22:21; 23:9).

decisions.choice: heard
decisions.reason: "The cry has come to me" means God has heard it. Readable says so.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה לְכָ֔ה וְאֶֽשְׁלָחֲךָ֖ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְהוֹצֵ֛א אֶת־עַמִּ֥י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And now go, and I will send you to Pharaoh, and bring out my people, [the] sons of Israel, from Egypt.

en.L: And now, go, and I will send you to Pharaoh, and bring {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, out of Egypt."
en.B: Go, then. I will send you to Pharaoh, and you are to bring {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, out of Egypt."
en.R: So now go. I am sending you to Pharaoh, the king. You will lead {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, out of Egypt."

es.L: Y ahora, ve, y yo te enviaré al faraón, y saca de Egipto a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, a los hijos de Israel».
es.B: Ve, pues. Te voy a enviar al faraón, y tú sacarás de Egipto a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, los israelitas».
es.R: Así que ahora ve. Te envío al faraón, el rey de Egipto. Tú sacarás de Egipto a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, los israelitas».

fr.L: Et maintenant, va, et je t’enverrai vers Pharaon, et fais sortir d’Égypte {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël. »
fr.B: Va donc. Je vais t’envoyer vers Pharaon, et tu feras sortir d’Égypte {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}. »
fr.R: Maintenant, va. Je t’envoie chez Pharaon, le roi. Tu feras sortir d’Égypte {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}. »

sw.L: Basi sasa, nenda, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitakutuma kwa Farao, uwatoe watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, wana wa Israeli, kutoka Misri."
sw.B: Basi nenda. Nitakutuma kwa Farao, nawe utawatoa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, Waisraeli, kutoka Misri."
sw.R: Kwa hiyo sasa nenda. Ninakutuma kwa Farao, mfalme wa Misri. Wewe utawaongoza watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, Waisraeli, watoke Misri."

vi.L: Và bây giờ, hãy đi, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ sai ngươi đến Pha-ra-ôn, và hãy đem dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên, ra khỏi Ai Cập."
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ con hãy đi. Ta sai con đến với Pha-ra-ôn để con đem dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là dân Y-sơ-ra-ên ra khỏi Ai Cập."
vi.R: Vậy bây giờ con hãy đi. Ta sai con đến gặp Pha-ra-ôn, vua Ai Cập. Con sẽ dẫn dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là dân Y-sơ-ra-ên ra khỏi Ai Cập."

ko.L: 그러니 이제 가거라. 내가 너를 바로에게 보낼 것이니, 내 백성 이스라엘 자손을 이집트에서 이끌어 내어라."
ko.B: 그러니 가거라. 내가 너를 바로에게 보내겠다. 너는 내 백성, 곧 이스라엘 백성을 이집트에서 이끌어 내어라."
ko.R: 그러니 이제 가거라. 내가 너를 이집트 왕 바로에게 보낸다. 너는 내 백성 이스라엘 사람들을 이집트에서 이끌어 낼 것이다."

pt.L: E agora vai, e eu te enviarei a Faraó, e tira o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo, os filhos de Israel, do Egito."
pt.B: Vai, pois. Eu te enviarei a Faraó, e tu tirarás do Egito o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo, os israelitas."
pt.R: Então agora vai. Eu estou te enviando a Faraó, o rei. Tu vais tirar do Egito o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo, os israelitas."

decisions.choice: I will send you ... bring out: God acts through Moses
decisions.reason: God says that he has come down to deliver Israel (verse 8), and that Moses will bring them out. Both are true: God works through the one he sends.

decisions.choice: bring out: the verb that gives the event its name
decisions.reason: "Bring out" of Egypt becomes the way the Old Testament speaks of the exodus (20:2).

decisions.choice: "đem ... ra khỏi", "dẫn ... ra khỏi" for bringing out
decisions.reason: The verb that names the event (meaning decision); Vietnamese keeps the plain verb of going out, which the later chapters repeat.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים מִ֣י אָנֹ֔כִי כִּ֥י אֵלֵ֖ךְ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְכִ֥י אוֹצִ֛יא אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses to God, who [am] I that I should go to Pharaoh and that I should bring out [the] sons of Israel from Egypt?

en.L: And Moses said to God, "Who [am] I, that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel out of Egypt?"
en.B: But Moses said to God, "Who am I to go to Pharaoh, and to bring the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of Egypt?"
en.R: But Moses said to God, "I am not important enough to go to Pharaoh. How can I lead the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of Egypt?"

es.L: Y dijo Moisés a Dios: «¿Quién [soy] yo, que vaya yo al faraón y que saque a los hijos de Israel de Egipto?».
es.B: Pero Moisés le dijo a Dios: «¿Quién soy yo para presentarme ante el faraón y sacar de Egipto a los israelitas?».
es.R: Pero Moisés le dijo a Dios: «Yo no soy lo bastante importante para ir a ver al faraón. ¿Cómo voy a sacar de Egipto a los israelitas?».

fr.L: Et Moïse dit à Dieu : « Qui [suis]-je, pour que j’aille vers Pharaon et que je fasse sortir d’Égypte les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël ? »
fr.B: Mais Moïse dit à Dieu : « Qui suis-je pour aller trouver Pharaon et faire sortir d’Égypte les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ? »
fr.R: Mais Moïse a dit à Dieu : « Je ne suis pas assez important pour aller voir Pharaon. Comment pourrais-je faire sortir les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} d’Égypte ? »

sw.L: Musa akamwambia Mungu, "Mimi [ni] nani, kwamba niende kwa Farao, na kwamba niwatoe wana wa Israeli katika Misri?"
sw.B: Lakini Musa akamwambia Mungu, "Mimi ni nani mpaka niweze kwenda kwa Farao na kuwaongoza Waisraeli watoke Misri?"
sw.R: Lakini Musa akamwambia Mungu, "Mimi si mtu wa maana kiasi cha kwenda kwa Farao. Nitawezaje kuwatoa Waisraeli Misri?"

vi.L: Và Môi-se thưa với Đức Chúa Trời: "Con [là] ai mà đi đến Pha-ra-ôn và đem con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên ra khỏi Ai Cập?"
vi.B: Nhưng Môi-se thưa với Đức Chúa Trời: "Con là ai mà dám đến gặp Pha-ra-ôn và đem dân Y-sơ-ra-ên ra khỏi Ai Cập?"
vi.R: Nhưng Môi-se thưa với Đức Chúa Trời: "Con chẳng là gì cả, sao có thể đến gặp Pha-ra-ôn? Làm sao con dẫn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên ra khỏi Ai Cập được?"

ko.L: 그리고 모세가 하나님께 말씀드렸다. "제가 누구[이기에] 바로에게 가며, 제가 이스라엘 자손을 이집트에서 이끌어 내겠습니까?"
ko.B: 그러나 모세가 하나님께 아뢰었다. "제가 무엇이기에 바로에게 가서 이스라엘 백성을 이집트에서 이끌어 낼 수 있겠습니까?"
ko.R: 그러나 모세가 하나님께 말씀드렸다. "저는 바로에게 갈 만한 사람이 못 됩니다. 제가 어떻게 이스라엘 사람들을 이집트에서 이끌어 낼 수 있겠습니까?"

pt.L: E Moisés disse a Deus: "Quem [sou] eu, para que vá a Faraó e para que tire os filhos de Israel do Egito?"
pt.B: Mas Moisés disse a Deus: "Quem sou eu para ir a Faraó e tirar os israelitas do Egito?"
pt.R: Mas Moisés disse a Deus: "Eu não sou importante o bastante para ir falar com Faraó. Como posso tirar os israelitas do Egito?"

decisions.choice: who am I: a question that means "I am not fit for this"
decisions.reason: The question is a protest, not a request for information. It is the first of five objections Moses makes (3:11, 13; 4:1, 10, 13). David asks the same question in 2 Samuel 7:18.

decisions.choice: I am not important enough
decisions.reason: Readable states the point of the question plainly.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ כִּֽי־אֶֽהְיֶ֣ה עִמָּ֔ךְ וְזֶה־לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת כִּ֥י אָנֹכִ֖י שְׁלַחְתִּ֑יךָ בְּהוֹצִֽיאֲךָ֤ אֶת־הָעָם֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם תַּֽעַבְדוּן֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים עַ֖ל הָהָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, for I will be with you, and this [will be] for you the sign that I sent you: when you bring out the people from Egypt, you will serve God on this mountain.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "For I will be with you; and this [will be] the sign for you that I have sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you will serve God on this mountain."
en.B: God answered, "I will be with you. And this will be your proof that I am the one who sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you will all worship God here on this mountain."
en.R: God said, "I will be with you. Here is how you will know that I have sent you. After you lead the people out of Egypt, all of you will come back here and worship God on this mountain."

es.L: Y dijo: «Porque yo estaré contigo; y esto [será] para ti la señal de que yo te he enviado: cuando hayas sacado al pueblo de Egipto, {{plural_you:servirán|serviréis}} a Dios sobre este monte».
es.B: Dios respondió: «Yo estaré contigo. Y esta será la prueba de que soy yo quien te envía: cuando hayas sacado al pueblo de Egipto, todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:adorarán|adoraréis}} a Dios aquí, en este monte».
es.R: Dios le dijo: «Yo estaré contigo. Así sabrás que yo te he enviado: después de que saques al pueblo de Egipto, todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:volverán|volveréis}} aquí y {{plural_you:adorarán|adoraréis}} a Dios en este monte».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Car je serai avec toi ; et ceci [sera] pour toi le signe que c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui t’ai envoyé : quand tu auras fait sortir le peuple d’Égypte, vous servirez Dieu sur cette montagne. »
fr.B: Dieu répondit : « Je serai avec toi. Et voici ce qui te prouvera que c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui t’ai envoyé : quand tu auras fait sortir le peuple d’Égypte, vous adorerez tous Dieu ici, sur cette montagne. »
fr.R: Dieu a dit : « Je serai avec toi. Voici comment tu sauras que c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui t’envoie. Quand tu auras fait sortir le peuple d’Égypte, vous reviendrez tous ici pour adorer Dieu sur cette montagne. »

sw.L: Akasema, "Kwa kuwa nitakuwa pamoja nawe; na hii [itakuwa] ishara kwako kwamba ni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niliyekutuma: utakapokuwa umewatoa watu Misri, mtamtumikia Mungu juu ya mlima huu."
sw.B: Mungu akajibu, "Nitakuwa pamoja nawe. Na hii itakuwa uthibitisho kwako kwamba ni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niliyekutuma: utakapowatoa watu Misri, ninyi nyote mtamwabudu Mungu hapa juu ya mlima huu."
sw.R: Mungu akasema, "Nitakuwa pamoja nawe. Hivi ndivyo utakavyojua kwamba ni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niliyekutuma. Baada ya kuwatoa watu Misri, ninyi nyote mtarudi hapa na kumwabudu Mungu juu ya mlima huu."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán: "Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ở với ngươi; và đây [sẽ là] dấu hiệu cho ngươi rằng chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã sai ngươi: khi ngươi đã đem dân ra khỏi Ai Cập, các ngươi sẽ phục vụ Đức Chúa Trời trên núi này."
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời đáp: "Ta sẽ ở với con. Và đây sẽ là dấu hiệu cho con biết chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã sai con: khi con đã đem dân ra khỏi Ai Cập, tất cả các con sẽ thờ phượng Đức Chúa Trời tại chính núi này."
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời phán: "Ta sẽ ở với con. Đây là cách con sẽ biết chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã sai con: Sau khi con dẫn dân ra khỏi Ai Cập, tất cả các con sẽ trở lại đây và thờ phượng Đức Chúa Trời trên núi này."

ko.L: 그러자 그분께서 말씀하셨다. "내가 너와 함께 있을 것이다. 그리고 이것이 내가 너를 보냈다는 너를 위한 표적[이 될 것이다]. 네가 그 백성을 이집트에서 이끌어 낸 뒤에, 너희가 이 산에서 하나님을 섬길 것이다."
ko.B: 하나님께서 대답하셨다. "내가 너와 함께 있겠다. 그리고 내가 너를 보냈다는 표적은 이것이다. 네가 백성을 이집트에서 이끌어 낸 뒤에, 너희가 모두 바로 이 산에서 하나님을 예배할 것이다."
ko.R: 하나님께서 말씀하셨다. "내가 너와 함께 있겠다. 내가 너를 보냈다는 것을 너는 이렇게 알게 될 것이다. 네가 백성을 이집트에서 이끌어 낸 뒤에, 너희가 모두 이리로 돌아와서 이 산에서 하나님을 예배할 것이다."

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse: "Porque eu estarei contigo; e este [será] para ti o sinal de que eu te enviei: quando tiveres tirado o povo do Egito, vocês servirão a Deus neste monte."
pt.B: Deus respondeu: "Eu estarei contigo. E esta será a prova de que fui eu quem te enviou: quando tiveres tirado o povo do Egito, todos vocês adorarão a Deus aqui neste monte."
pt.R: Deus disse: "Eu estarei contigo. Assim saberás que fui eu quem te enviou: depois que tirares o povo do Egito, todos vocês vão voltar aqui e adorar a Deus neste monte."

decisions.choice: I will be: the verb of the name in verse 14
decisions.reason: "I will be with you" uses the same verb form that God uses of himself in verse 14. The answer to Moses' "Who am I?" is not who Moses is, but who will be with him.

decisions.choice: this will be the sign: the sign comes after the event
alternatives: the burning bush is the sign
decisions.reason: The sign is the worship on this mountain, which can come only after the exodus. It may be a sign that confirms afterward, or "this" may point back to the burning bush as the present sign. The first reading fits the words best.

decisions.choice: you will serve God: worship him
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of Israel's forced labor for Egypt (1:13-14). Israel will move from serving Pharaoh to serving God (4:23; 7:16).

decisions.choice: you will all / all of you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" is plural: Moses and the people. Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: "yo estaré contigo"
decisions.reason: Spanish must choose between its two verbs "to be". Being with someone is "estar", while the name in verse 14 uses "ser" ("YO SOY"). The Hebrew uses one verb for both, so the echo between this promise and the name (m1) is weaker in Spanish; see the decision at verse 14.

decisions.choice: "표적" (sign)
decisions.reason: Korean Psalms 78 and 105 and Acts 7:36 call the signs in Egypt "표적"; the same word is kept through Exodus 3-11.

decisions.choice: "내가 너와 함께 있을 것이다" (I will be with you)
decisions.reason: Literal uses "있다", the verb Korean uses for the name in verse 14, so the link the meaning decision notes can still be heard.

decisions.choice: "phục vụ" (L); "thờ phượng" (B, R)
decisions.reason: To serve God here is to worship him (meaning decision); Literal keeps the verb used of slavery in Egypt, so the reader sees the change of master.

decisions.choice: servirão a Deus (L); adorarão a Deus (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "servir", the verb of Israel's forced labor in 1:13-14, so that the move from serving Pharaoh to serving God (m3) can be heard; Balanced and Readable say "adorar", as the English says "worship".

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־הָֽאֱלֹהִ֗ים הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֣י בָא֮ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וְאָמַרְתִּ֣י לָהֶ֔ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם שְׁלָחַ֣נִי אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וְאָֽמְרוּ־לִ֣י מַה־שְּׁמ֔וֹ מָ֥ה אֹמַ֖ר אֲלֵהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses to God, look, I [am] coming to [the] sons of Israel and I say to them, [the] God of your fathers has sent me to you, and they say to me, what [is] his name? What shall I say to them?

en.L: And Moses said to God, "Look, I am coming to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and I will say to them, 'The God of your fathers has sent me to you,' and they will say to me, 'What [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name?' What shall I say to them?"
en.B: Moses said to God, "Suppose I go to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and tell them, 'The God of your fathers has sent me to you,' and they ask me, 'What is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name?' What answer am I to give them?"
en.R: Moses said to God, "Suppose I go to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and say, 'The God of your ancestors has sent me to you.' They will ask me, 'What is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name?' What should I tell them?"

es.L: Y dijo Moisés a Dios: «He aquí, yo voy a los hijos de Israel y les diré: “El Dios de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} padres me ha enviado a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}”, y ellos me dirán: “¿Cuál [es] {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre?”. ¿Qué les diré?».
es.B: Moisés le dijo a Dios: «Supongamos que voy a los israelitas y les digo: “El Dios de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} padres me ha enviado a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}”, y ellos me preguntan: “¿Cuál es {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre?”. ¿Qué les voy a responder?».
es.R: Moisés le dijo a Dios: «Supongamos que voy a los israelitas y les digo: “El Dios de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} antepasados me ha enviado a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}”. Ellos me van a preguntar: “¿Cuál es {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre?”. ¿Qué les debo decir?».

fr.L: Et Moïse dit à Dieu : « Voici, je vais vers les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, et je leur dirai : “Le Dieu de vos pères m’a envoyé vers vous”, et ils me diront : “Quel [est] {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom ?” Que leur dirai-je ? »
fr.B: Moïse dit à Dieu : « Admettons que j’aille trouver les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} et que je leur dise : “Le Dieu de vos pères m’a envoyé vers vous”, et qu’ils me demandent : “Quel est {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom ?” Que devrai-je leur répondre ? »
fr.R: Moïse a dit à Dieu : « Imaginons que j’aille voir les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} et que je leur dise : “Le Dieu de vos ancêtres m’a envoyé vers vous.” Ils vont me demander : “Quel est {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom ?” Qu’est-ce que je leur dirai ? »

sw.L: Musa akamwambia Mungu, "Tazama, ninakwenda kwa wana wa Israeli, nami nitawaambia, 'Mungu wa baba zenu amenituma kwenu,' nao wataniambia, 'Jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} [ni] nani?' Nitawaambia nini?"
sw.B: Musa akamwambia Mungu, "Tuseme nimekwenda kwa Waisraeli na kuwaambia, 'Mungu wa baba zenu amenituma kwenu,' nao wakaniuliza, 'Jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} ni nani?' Nitawajibu nini?"
sw.R: Musa akamwambia Mungu, "Tuseme ninakwenda kwa Waisraeli na kuwaambia, 'Mungu wa mababu zenu amenituma kwenu.' Wataniuliza, 'Jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} ni nani?' Niwaambie nini?"

vi.L: Và Môi-se thưa với Đức Chúa Trời: "Kìa, con đến cùng con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên và nói với họ: 'Đức Chúa Trời của tổ phụ các ngươi đã sai ta đến với các ngươi,' và họ hỏi con: 'Danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [là] gì?' thì con sẽ nói gì với họ?"

decisions.choice: I am who I am: God's name explained from the verb "to be"
alternatives: I will be who I will be
I am the one who is (Septuagint)
I will be what I will be
decisions.reason: The divine name in verse 15 sounds like this verb. The Hebrew verb form can mean "I am" or "I will be", so the phrase may mean "I am who I am" (God is who he is, not defined by anything else), "I will be who I will be" (God will show who he is by what he does), or "I am the one who is" (the Septuagint). Verse 12, "I will be with you", uses the same form and points to God's presence with his people. The words are kept as close to the Hebrew as possible so that the reader can weigh these senses.

decisions.choice: I AM has sent me: the verb is used as a name
decisions.reason: The first word of the phrase stands alone as the name of the one who sends Moses. In verse 15 God gives the name itself, which sounds like it.

decisions.choice: I AM WHO I AM; I AM
decisions.reason: Capitals mark the words as God's name, as "LORD" is marked. The present tense is kept as the best-known English form; the footnote gives "I will be".

decisions.choice: the one called I AM
decisions.reason: Readable says that "I AM" is used as a name.

decisions.choice: «YO SOY QUIEN SOY»; «YO SOY» used as a name
alternatives: «YO SOY EL QUE SOY» (the traditional Spanish form)
decisions.reason: As in English, capitals mark the words as God's name, and the present tense is kept, with "I will be" in the footnote (m1). "Quien soy" is the plain modern Spanish for "who I am" and leaves the phrase as open as the Hebrew. The name uses "ser", who God is; the promise of verse 12 needed "estar" ("yo estaré contigo"), so Spanish cannot echo verse 12 with the same verb as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: « JE SUIS QUI JE SUIS »; « JE SUIS » used as a name
alternatives: « Je suis celui qui suis » (the traditional French form)
decisions.reason: As in English, capitals mark the words as God's name, and the present tense is kept, with "I will be" in the footnote (m1). "Qui je suis" is the plain modern French for "who I am" and leaves the phrase as open as the Hebrew; the traditional "celui qui suis" sounds old-fashioned and leans toward one reading. French uses one verb "être" here and in verse 12 ("je serai avec toi"), so the echo between the promise and the name comes through.

decisions.choice: "NIKO NILIYE"; "NIKO" used as a name
alternatives: "NITAKUWA NITAKAVYOKUWA" (I will be what I will be)
decisions.reason: As in English, capitals mark the words as God's name. "Niko" (I am, I am here) is the verb of being and of presence, which fits the promise of verse 12 ("nitakuwa pamoja nawe", I will be with you), and it is short enough to stand alone as a name ("NIKO amenituma kwenu"). "Niliye" (I who am) says "who I am" without the heavier "ambaye". Swahili cannot keep the possible future sense in the same words; the footnote gives "I will be who I will be". A native reviewer should judge whether this or the familiar wording reads better.

decisions.choice: "나는 있는 나다" for "I AM WHO I AM", and "'나는 있다' 하시는 분" for "I AM" as a name
decisions.reason: Built from "있다" (to be), the verb Korean John 8:58 uses for "I am", so the name and its explanation stay linked as the English and its meaning decision link them; the familiar Korean wordings belong to copyrighted or archaic versions and were not followed.

decisions.choice: "TA LÀ ĐẤNG TA LÀ"; "TA LÀ" (L), "Đấng TA LÀ" (B) as a name
alternatives: Ta là Đấng Tự Hữu Hằng Hữu
decisions.reason: The terms note asks this verse to follow the English wording: the name is explained from the verb "to be" (meaning decision, footnoted), and "là" is that verb. "Đấng Hằng Hữu" (the Ever-Existing One), used for the echo of this verse in John 8, explains the name rather than giving it; a reviewer may prefer it.

decisions.choice: EU SOU O QUE SOU; EU SOU
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1) and docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md ask for 3:14-15: the words are written in capitals because they are used as God's name, as "SENHOR" is, and in the present tense; the meaning note gives the other readings, "I will be who I will be" ("Serei o que serei") among them (m1). "O que" keeps the open, unexplained sense of the Hebrew relative better than "quem". Readable says that "EU SOU" is used as a name, as the English Readable does (r-en-2).

ko.B: 하나님께서 모세에게 또 말씀하셨다. "이스라엘 백성에게 이렇게 말하여라. '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 곧 너희 조상들의 하나님, 아브라함과 이삭과 야곱의 하나님께서 나를 너희에게 보내셨다.' 이것이 영원한 내 이름이며, 모든 세대가 나를 기억하며 부를 이름이다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 모세에게 또 말씀하셨다. "이스라엘 사람들에게 이렇게 말하여라. '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 곧 여러분 조상들의 하나님께서 저를 여러분에게 보내셨습니다. 그분은 아브라함과 이삭과 야곱의 하나님이십니다.' 이것이 영원한 내 이름이다. 모든 세대의 사람들이 이 이름으로 나를 기억할 것이다.

pt.L: E Deus disse ainda a Moisés: "Assim dirás aos filhos de Israel: '{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus dos pais de vocês, o Deus de Abraão, o Deus de Isaque e o Deus de Jacó, me enviou a vocês.' Este [é] o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome para sempre, e esta [é] a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} lembrança de geração em geração.
pt.B: Deus disse também a Moisés: "Dirás aos israelitas: '{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus dos pais de vocês, o Deus de Abraão, de Isaque e de Jacó, me enviou a vocês.' Este é o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome para sempre, o nome pelo qual serei lembrado em todas as gerações.
pt.R: Deus disse ainda a Moisés: "Dirás aos israelitas: '{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus dos antepassados de vocês, me enviou a vocês. Ele é o Deus de Abraão, de Isaque e de Jacó.' Este é o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome para sempre. As pessoas de todas as gerações vão se lembrar de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} por este nome.

decisions.choice: Yahweh: the personal name of God
decisions.reason: The four letters of the name sound like the verb "to be" of verse 14, and may mean "he is" or "he causes to be". Out of reverence, Jews came to read it aloud as "Lord" (Adonai). The exact pronunciation is not certain; "Yahweh" is the usual scholarly form.

decisions.choice: my remembrance: the name by which I am to be called on
decisions.reason: "Remembrance" is the name spoken in worship (Psalm 135:13; Hosea 12:5). This name is to be used for all generations.

decisions.choice: this is my name forever: the name is given for all time
decisions.reason: God's name is not a secret to be kept; it is given to his people to use.

decisions.choice: the LORD; with the setting, Yahweh
decisions.reason: The name is written "the LORD" by default, following the long tradition of reading it as "Lord". The divine name setting gives "Yahweh".

decisions.choice: "el SEÑOR" (default); "Yahvé" with the divine name setting
decisions.reason: As in English, the name is written "el SEÑOR" in capitals by default, following the long tradition of reading it as "Lord"; the setting gives "Yahvé", the usual Spanish form of the name. Only "Yahvé" lets the reader hear that the name sounds like the verb of verse 14 (m1). "Jehová", the form of the Reina-Valera tradition, is not used (see 3:2).

decisions.choice: "le SEIGNEUR" (default); "Yahvé" with the divine name setting
decisions.reason: As in English, the name is written "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals by default, following the long tradition of reading it as "Lord"; the setting gives "Yahvé", the usual French form of the name, which lets the reader hear that it sounds like the verb of verse 14 (m1). "L'Éternel", used since the Reformation in French Protestant Bibles, also tries to carry the link with "to be"; a reviewer may prefer it (see 3:2).

decisions.choice: "BWANA" (default); "Yahwe" with the divine name setting
decisions.reason: As in English, the name is written "BWANA" (Lord) in capitals by default, following the long tradition of reading it as "Lord"; the setting gives "Yahwe", the name written in Swahili spelling. In neither form can a Swahili reader hear the link with "NIKO" in verse 14; the meaning decision explains it.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}" here, where the name itself is given
decisions.reason: Here the English keeps its divine_name span and its decision, and Korean does the same: by default "주" (the LORD), and with the setting the name "야훼". "여호와" is not used, as the Korean style guide (7a) sets.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}": "CHÚA" by default, "Gia-vê" with the setting
decisions.reason: Where the name itself is the subject, as here, the setting matters most: the default follows the English "the LORD" in capitals, and the alternative gives the name as most scholars think it was said, as the Vietnamese style guide settles. "Đức Giê-hô-va", the older Protestant form, is not used.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1) and docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md: here the name itself is given, and "o SENHOR" follows the tradition of reading it as "Lord"; the setting shows "Javé", the usual Brazilian form. Neither form lets a Portuguese reader hear the link with "EU SOU" in verse 14 (m1); the meaning note explains it.

records.literal_gloss: Go, and gather [the] elders of Israel and say to them, Yahweh, [the] God of your fathers, has appeared to me, [the] God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, saying, visiting I have visited you and what is done to you in Egypt,

en.L: Go and gather the elders of Israel and say to them, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, has appeared to me, saying, "I have surely visited you and [seen] what is done to you in Egypt,
en.B: Go and call together the elders of Israel and tell them, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, appeared to me. He said, "I have come to your aid, and I have taken note of how you are treated in Egypt.
en.R: Go and bring together the leaders of Israel. Tell them, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors, came to me. He is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He said, "I have been watching over you. I have seen how the Egyptians are treating you.

es.L: Ve y reúne a los ancianos de Israel y diles: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} padres, el Dios de Abraham, de Isaac y de Jacob, se me ha aparecido, diciendo: ‘Ciertamente {{plural_you:los|os}} he visitado y [he visto] lo que se {{plural_you:les|os}} hace en Egipto,
es.B: Ve y convoca a los ancianos de Israel, y diles: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} padres, el Dios de Abraham, de Isaac y de Jacob, se me apareció. Me dijo: ‘He venido en {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} ayuda, y he visto cómo {{plural_you:los|os}} tratan en Egipto.
es.R: Ve y reúne a los líderes de Israel. Diles: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} antepasados, vino a mí. Él es el Dios de Abraham, de Isaac y de Jacob. Me dijo: ‘He estado cuidando de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. He visto cómo {{plural_you:los|os}} tratan los egipcios.
